objective.value: Develop a general strategy combining retrobiosynthesis and a precursor selection step to design biosynthetic pathways for 15 short-chain primary amines (SCPAs), and construct platform E. coli strains producing SCPAs first from fed amino-acid precursors and then de novo from glucose, including enhanced iso-butylamine and ethylamine production.
objective.notes: Scope limited to SCPAs C1-C7; tert-butylamine and aniline dropped after precursor selection (results_p004).

hypothesis.value: Amino acids are ideal precursors for SCPAs because their pathways are well characterized and carry high flux; a sufficiently promiscuous PLP-dependent decarboxylase (S. viridifaciens VlmD, EC 4.1.1.-) can convert selected amino-acid precursors to the corresponding SCPAs, and irreversible decarboxylation provides a strong flux-driving force.
hypothesis.notes: Author-stated hypotheses; irreversibility rationale supported by literature analogy (refs 25-27), not by direct thermodynamic measurement in this study.

strain.value: Production host: E. coli WL3110 (lacI knockout mutant of W3110). Enzyme overexpression host: E. coli BL21(DE3). Cloning host: E. coli NEB 10-beta. Precursor-overproducing chassis: E. coli Val (pKBRilvBNCED) (L-valine overproducer, constructed previously, ref 21) and its parent WLGBH (intact ilvA/leuA/panB). Engineered strains: PA01, EA01, iBA01, iAA01, iBA02, and 12 EA01-derived VlmD-variant strains. Controls: NC01, NC02, NC03.
strain.notes: Complete strain/plasmid list deferred to Supplementary Table 2 (not available in this payload); NC01 exact genotype requires_supplement.

genotype.value: PA01 = WL3110 / pTac15-vlmDopt (codon-optimized S. viridifaciens vlmD in pTac15K, EcoRI/KpnI). EA01 = WL3110 / pTac15-vlmDopt-alaDopt (codon-optimized G. stearothermophilus alaD, KpnI/PstI). iBA01 = Val (pKBRilvBNCED) / pTac15-vlmDopt; Val background carries deletions ilvA, leuA, panB (auxotrophic for L-Ile, L-Leu, D-pantothenate). iAA01 = iBA01 + pTac-driven leuABCD overexpression. iBA02 = WLGBH (pKBRilvBNCED) / pTac15-vlmDopt-anti-ilvA-leuA-panB (sRNA knockdown cassettes). VlmD variants: V94I, V94L, V114I, V114L, T397A, T397V, W399L, S431T, S431V, S431L, D515K, D515N on pTac15-vlmDopt-alaDopt. NC02 = Val (pKBRilvBNCED) with empty plasmid (no vlmD). NC03 = L-leucine-producing strain without vlmD.
genotype.notes: pKBRilvBNCED carries ilvBNCED overexpression (per Fig. 6 gene labels). Codon-optimized gene sequences in Supplementary Table 4 (unavailable). WLGBH full genotype requires_supplement.

engineering_method.value: Computational retrobiosynthesis (in-house tool, 84 SMARTS reaction rules) + precursor selection (PubChem MeSH Tree via PubChemPy; RDT v1.5.1 functional-group position analysis); heterologous expression of codon-optimized vlmD and alaD on pTac15K plasmids; overexpression of leuABCD; synthetic sRNA knockdown of ilvA/leuA/panB (Gibson-assembled cassettes, method per ref 32); rational protein engineering via SWISS-MODEL homology modeling (template GAD67, PDB 2OKJ) + AutoDock Vina docking + BLASTP homolog-scanning to nominate 12 single mutations introduced by site-directed mutagenesis; fed-batch fermentation optimization.
engineering_method.notes: The ilvA/leuA/panB gene deletions in the Val chassis were performed in a previous study (ref 21) - background, not this paper's engineering action.

experimental_groups.value: (1) In vitro: purified His-VlmD + each of 13 amino-acid precursors (incl. glycine). (2) In vivo feeding: PA01 fed 2 g/L of each of 12 precursors individually. (3) De novo flask: NC01 vs EA01 (ethylamine); NC02 vs iBA01 (iso-butylamine); NC03 vs iAA01 (iso-amylamine). (4) Fed-batch: iBA01 in NM3 with Ile/Leu/pantothenate; iBA02 in NM3 without supplementation. (5) Enzyme engineering: EA01 plus 12 single-mutation VlmD-variant strains, flask ethylamine production.
experimental_groups.notes: Groups instantiated per experiment; no paper-level unified condition.

controls.value: In vitro: reactions without VlmD (no-enzyme controls, black chromatograms in Fig. 3). De novo flask: NC01 (control for EA01, exact genotype requires Supplementary Table 2), NC02 = Val (pKBRilvBNCED) harboring empty plasmid without vlmD (control for iBA01), NC03 = L-leucine-producing strain without vlmD (control for iAA01). Fed-batch comparison: iBA01 with supplementation serves as reference for iBA02. Enzyme engineering: EA01 with native VlmD as baseline for the 12 variants.
controls.notes: Controls instantiated per experiment; NC01 identity only indicated as 'control' in Fig. 6 caption - blocked_pending_supplement for exact genotype.

culture_conditions.value: Flask: seed in 10 mL LB at 37 C for 8 h; 1.5 mL seed into 50 mL medium in 300 mL baffled flask; PA01 at 37 C, 200 rpm, 36 h; EA01 at 37 C, 200 rpm, 48 h; iBA01/iAA01 at 30 C, 200 rpm, 48 h. Enzyme overexpression: BL21(DE3)/pET-his-vlmDopt in 200 mL LB at 37 C, 1 mM IPTG induction after 3 h, harvest after further 5 h. Fed-batch: 6.6 L Bioflo 3000 with 2 L NM3, 30 C, pH 7.0 (28% ammonia), air 2 L/min, DO 40% via agitation 200-1000 rpm + pure O2, 100 mL feeding solution added when residual glucose < 3 g/L.
culture_conditions.notes: iBA02 fed-batch run under same conditions as iBA01 minus Ile/Leu/pantothenate.

medium.value: MR medium (pH 7.0; per L: 6.67 g KH2PO4, 4 g (NH4)2HPO4, 0.8 g MgSO4.7H2O, 0.8 g citric acid, 5 mL trace metal solution) + 10 g/L glucose + 2 g/L amino-acid precursor for PA01; MR + 20 g/L glucose for EA01. NM2 medium (per ref 21; 50 g/L glucose, 30 g/L CaCO3, 12.5 g/L (NH4)2SO4, 4.0 g/L KH2PO4, 2.0 g/L MgSO4.7H2O, yeast extract, 0.262 g/L L-Ile, 0.262 g/L L-Leu, 0.425 mg/L sodium D-pantothenate, 5 mL trace metal) for iBA01; NM2 without L-leucine for iAA01. NM3 for fed-batch (20 g/L glucose, 20 g/L (NH4)2SO4, 2 g/L KH2PO4, 0.4 g/L MgSO4.7H2O, 1.6 g/L NaCl, 5 g/L yeast extract, 0.262 g/L L-Ile, 0.262 g/L L-Leu, 0.362 mg/L sodium D-pantothenate, 5 mL trace metal). Feeding solution: 400 g/L glucose, 20 g/L KH2PO4, 2.1 g/L L-Ile, 2.1 g/L L-Leu, 3.62 mg/L sodium D-pantothenate. LB for cloning/seed.
medium.notes: NM2 composition in parsed text contains OCR artifacts ('2 g LaO4' repeated three times; yeast extract quantity lost) - exact reproduction blocked pending original PDF/Supplement; see conflicts.

dosage.value: Precursor feeding 2 g/L (each of 12 precursors, individually). In vitro assay: 1 mM amino-acid precursor, 0.1 mM PLP, 150 ug/mL purified His-VlmD in 50 mM potassium phosphate pH 7.5. IPTG 1 mM. Antibiotics: kanamycin 25 ug/mL, ampicillin 50 ug/mL. Fed-batch feeding solution composition and trigger (<3 g/L residual glucose) as above.

time.value: In vitro enzymatic reaction 2 h at 37 C. Shake-flask cultivation: PA01 36 h; EA01 48 h; iBA01/iAA01 48 h. Seed cultures 8 h (flask) / 7 h (fed-batch seed). Induction: IPTG at 3 h post-inoculation, harvest 5 h later. Fed-batch duration not stated numerically in main text (profiles in Fig. 7).
time.notes: Exact fed-batch run time requires reading Fig. 7 axis (not numerically in text).

replicates.value: In vitro enzyme assays in triplicates; in vivo SCPA production experiments in triplicates; all flask cultures repeated three times; mean +/- s.d. iBA02 fed-batch reproduced once (second profile in Supplementary Fig. 5); replicate count for iBA01 fed-batch not stated.
replicates.notes: Replicate type (biological vs technical/independent cultures) not explicitly defined - replicate_type unresolved; 'repeated three times' most consistent with independent culture replicates but not author-labeled.

assay.value: SCPA quantification by HPLC with automatic pre-column OPA derivatization (C18, 25 C, gradient elution, detection 230 nm); identity confirmation by LC-MS after AccQ-Tag Ultra derivatization (ESI positive, 50-500 m/z); cell growth OD600; glucose by enzymatic analyzer; protein concentration by Bio-Rad Protein Assay (BSA standard).

instruments.value: Agilent 1100 Series HPLC with Eclipse plus C18 column (4.6 x 150 mm) and G1314A variable wavelength detector; Agilent LC/MSD VL with Waters XBridge C18 (5 um, 4.6 x 150 mm); Ultrospec 3000 spectrophotometer; YSI 2700 STAT glucose analyzer; Bioflo 3000 6.6 L bioreactor; Sonics VCX-600 ultrasonic homogenizer; Talon metal affinity resin; Amicon Ultra-15 (10 kDa).

analysis_methods.value: Agilent ChemStation 4.03 data collection; Microsoft Excel 2013 and OriginPro 2019 analysis; mean +/- s.d. over triplicates (no formal hypothesis tests reported). Computational: in-house retrobiosynthesis tool with 84 SMARTS reaction rules derived from KEGG third-level EC numbers (ChemAxon Reactor JChem 19.9.0 named as alternative); PubChemPy v1.0.4 MeSH Tree lookup; RDT v1.5.1; SWISS-MODEL homology modeling; AutoDock Vina v1.1.2 docking; BLASTP v2.10.1 against nr (250 homologous sequences).
analysis_methods.notes: No statistical significance testing reported; fold-changes and percent improvements are descriptive.

outcomes.value: In vitro: VlmD converted 12/13 precursors (glycine->methylamine failed); near or above 80% conversion for L-2-aminobutyrate, L-norvaline, L-valine, L-isovaline, L-isoleucine, 1-aminocyclohexanecarboxylic acid. In vivo feeding (PA01): 10/12 SCPAs produced (ethylamine 76.28, n-propylamine 873.31, iso-propylamine 337.57, n-butylamine 979.17, iso-butylamine 1289.18, (R)-sec-butylamine 936.70, iso-amylamine 1052.36, 2-methylbutylamine 1015.75, cyclopentylamine 264.03, cyclohexylamine 105.82 mg/L); n-amylamine and benzylamine not produced (precursors L-norleucine and L-2-phenylglycine poorly utilized). De novo from glucose: EA01 2.89 mg/L ethylamine with 22.78 mg/L L-alanine byproduct; iBA01 1155.74 mg/L iso-butylamine with no L-valine byproduct (vs 524.91 mg/L L-valine for NC02); iAA01 93.23 mg/L iso-amylamine with 991.23 mg/L L-leucine and 759.89 mg/L iso-butylamine byproducts. Fed-batch: iBA01 8.63 g/L iso-butylamine (productivity 0.21 g/L/h, yield 0.062 g/g); iBA02 10.67 g/L (0.36 g/L/h, yield 0.057 g/g, max OD600 60.5 vs 37.9 for iBA01) without amino-acid/vitamin supplementation. Enzyme engineering: V94I variant 5.69 mg/L ethylamine, 96.9% above EA01.
outcomes.notes: Author interpretations flagged as inference: 'VlmD has a strong driving force' (results_p034) and byproduct-attribution reasoning for iAA01 (results_p037, uses 'likely/might') are author_interpretation, not causally validated.

experiments.purpose: Design biosynthetic pathways for 15 SCPAs: retrobiosynthesis (84 reaction rules) followed by precursor selection (molecular type = amino acid; functional-group relative position matching VlmD's known substrates).
experiments.intervention: Computational pathway design; no wet-lab intervention.
experiments.conditions: In-house retrobiosynthesis tool; PubChemPy MeSH Tree; RDT v1.5.1; code at bitbucket.org/kaistsystemsbiology/retro-precursor-selection.
experiments.readout: 4-21 predicted precursors per SCPA; best amino-acid precursor identified for 13/15 SCPAs; tert-butylamine and aniline excluded (no suitable amino-acid precursor).
experiments.analysis: Retrosynthesis + structural filtering; all amino-acid precursors mapped to EC 4.1.1.- (reaction rule #51).
experiments.outcome: Pathway designs for 13 SCPAs; VlmD selected as proof-of-concept promiscuous decarboxylase.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass (active design choice defining all subsequent constructs), Q2 pass (this study updated reaction rules and ran the analysis), Q3 pass (determined which precursors/enzyme were tested downstream).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Pathway design/elucidation: retrobiosynthesis identified single-step decarboxylation routes and the precursor selection step fixed the amino-acid precursor per SCPA.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Bio-based SCPA production absent despite industrial need; retrobiosynthesis predicted single enzymatic conversion from amino-acid precursors for all 15 SCPAs.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Computational prediction (retrobiosynthesis tool + database filters); predictive, required experimental confirmation which was obtained downstream (EXP-01/02).
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper explicitly states the rationale: amino-acid pathways are well characterized and carry high flux; decarboxylation irreversibility provides a driving force; functional-group position relative to the reaction center affects reaction feasibility and enzyme active-site binding.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When designing biosynthetic routes for a family of structurally related chemicals in E. coli, filter retrobiosynthesis-predicted precursors to amino acids whose amine/carboxyl groups sit at the same positions relative to the reaction-center carbon as the chosen promiscuous decarboxylase's known substrates, because amino-acid metabolism sustains high precursor flux and matched functional-group geometry preserves catalytic compatibility.
alternatives_considered: amino alcohols, other SCPAs and alkyl-CoA precursors - rejected: poorly characterized pathways
hydrocarbon precursors - rejected: short-chain hydrocarbon production considered harder than amino acids
tert-butylamine and aniline - dropped: no amino-acid precursor with matching functional-group positions

experiments.purpose: Validate retrobiosynthesis/precursor selection in vitro: test purified His-tagged VlmD against 13 amino-acid precursors.
experiments.host: Cell-free assay; enzyme produced in E. coli BL21(DE3)/pET-his-vlmDopt
experiments.intervention: None on production host; enzyme purification and assay only.
experiments.conditions: 50 mM potassium phosphate pH 7.5, 1 mM substrate, 0.1 mM PLP, 150 ug/mL VlmD, 2 h at 37 C.
experiments.control: Reactions without VlmD (no-enzyme control per panel).
experiments.readout: HPLC conversion %; product identity by LC-MS (Supplementary Fig. 2).
experiments.outcome: 12/13 precursors converted; glycine->methylamine no detectable activity; six substrates >= ~80% conversion.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 fail: pure measurement/characterization of an already-selected enzyme; no engineering modification of host or pathway in this step.

experiments.purpose: Establish platform strain PA01 expressing codon-optimized vlmD and test in vivo SCPA production by feeding 12 direct precursors (2 g/L each).
experiments.host: E. coli WL3110 (lacI- mutant of W3110)
experiments.intervention: Transformation with pTac15-vlmDopt (heterologous codon-optimized S. viridifaciens vlmD under Ptac in pTac15K).
experiments.conditions: MR medium pH 7.0 + 10 g/L glucose + 2 g/L precursor; 37 C, 200 rpm, 36 h, 50 mL in 300 mL baffled flask.
experiments.control: No separate negative-control strain stated for the feeding panel in main text.
experiments.replicates: Triplicates per SCPA (independent flask cultures; type not author-specified).
experiments.readout: SCPA titers by HPLC-OPA; residual precursor for the two failures (Supplementary Fig. 3).
experiments.outcome: 10/12 SCPAs produced in vivo (titers 76.28-1289.18 mg/L); n-amylamine and benzylamine not produced due to poor precursor utilization (L-norleucine 1.92, L-2-phenylglycine 1.82 g/L remaining of 2 g/L).

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass (heterologous expression construct), Q2 pass (pTac15-vlmDopt constructed in this study), Q3 pass (platform strain defined all downstream de novo work).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Installation of the terminal heterologous decarboxylation step (pathway construction) in the production host.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Retrobiosynthesis predicted EC 4.1.1.- decarboxylation of amino-acid precursors; VlmD previously reported (ref 28) to convert L-Val/L-Leu/L-Ile to three SCPAs, suggesting exploitable promiscuity.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Decision validated by measured in vivo titers for 10/12 SCPAs and by in vitro conversion data.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper explicitly argues irreversible decarboxylation serves as a driving force for strong flux (citing refs 25-27) and selects VlmD for reported substrate promiscuity.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When building a platform E. coli strain for a group of related short-chain primary amines, terminate each pathway with a single promiscuous PLP-dependent decarboxylase acting on amino-acid precursors, because irreversible decarboxylation provides a thermodynamic driving force toward amine formation.
alternatives_considered: other EC 4.1.1.- enzymes - noted as examinable but not tested

experiments.purpose: De novo ethylamine production from glucose.
experiments.intervention: Co-overexpression of codon-optimized G. stearothermophilus alaD (alanine dehydrogenase, pyruvate -> L-alanine) with vlmDopt (strain EA01, plasmid pTac15-vlmDopt-alaDopt).
experiments.conditions: MR + 20 g/L glucose; 37 C, 200 rpm, 48 h flask.
experiments.control: NC01 (control strain; exact genotype requires Supplementary Table 2).
experiments.outcome: 2.89 mg/L ethylamine; 22.78 mg/L L-alanine byproduct (> ethylamine titer), attributed by authors to insufficient VlmD activity toward L-alanine.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass (heterologous alaD overexpression), Q2 pass (constructed here), Q3 pass (revealed precursor/conversion imbalance motivating VlmD engineering, EXP-08).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Precursor supply: alaD channels pyruvate to L-alanine, the direct precursor of ethylamine.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Feeding-based production requires externally supplied L-alanine; de novo production needs endogenous L-alanine supply from glucose.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: alaD choice follows its prior use for L-alanine production in engineered E. coli (ref 31); paper states the enzymatic function but not a deeper mechanistic selection rationale.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When producing an L-alanine-derived amine from glucose in E. coli, overexpress alanine dehydrogenase (alaD) to supply the L-alanine precursor directly from pyruvate, because alaD catalyzes reductive amination of pyruvate to L-alanine.

experiments.purpose: De novo iso-butylamine production from glucose.
experiments.host: E. coli Val (pKBRilvBNCED) - L-valine overproducer constructed previously (ref 21)
experiments.intervention: Transformation of Val (pKBRilvBNCED) with pTac15-vlmDopt (strain iBA01). The L-valine-overproducing chassis itself (ilvA/leuA/panB deletions, pKBRilvBNCED) is background from ref 21, not this paper's action.
experiments.conditions: NM2 medium; 30 C, 200 rpm, 48 h flask.
experiments.control: NC02 = Val (pKBRilvBNCED) with empty plasmid (no vlmD).
experiments.outcome: 1155.74 mg/L (15.80 mM) iso-butylamine, no L-valine byproduct; exceeds NC02 L-valine titer (524.91 mg/L). Identified problem: Val strain auxotrophic for L-Ile, L-Leu, D-pantothenate.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass for the new action (introducing vlmD into the Val chassis); the chassis engineering fails Q2 and is treated as background, not annotated.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Installation of the terminal decarboxylation step into a precursor-overproducing host, redirecting L-valine flux to iso-butylamine.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: PA01 feeding gave the highest in vivo titer for iso-butylamine (1289.18 mg/L), and an L-valine-overproducing chassis was already available.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured titers in flask, later confirmed in fed-batch.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper explicitly states the Val (pKBRilvBNCED) strain and plasmid were previously developed/obtained from the earlier study (ref 21); the design step is reuse of an existing overproducer chassis.

experiments.purpose: De novo iso-amylamine production from glucose.
experiments.intervention: Additional overexpression of leuABCD (L-leucine biosynthesis) on pTac15-vlmDopt-pTac-leuABCD (strain iAA01).
experiments.conditions: NM2 without L-leucine; 30 C, 200 rpm, 48 h flask.
experiments.readout: Iso-amylamine, L-leucine, iso-butylamine titers (Fig. 6c, Supplementary Fig. 4).
experiments.outcome: 93.23 mg/L iso-amylamine; byproducts 991.23 mg/L L-leucine and 759.89 mg/L iso-butylamine. Authors attribute L-leucine accumulation to suboptimal VlmD conversion and iso-butylamine to VlmD preference for L-valine generated from 2-ketoisovalerate (author_interpretation, 'likely/might' - not causally validated).

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass (leuABCD overexpression), Q2 pass (constructed here), Q3 pass (revealed VlmD substrate-preference bottleneck informing future work).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Precursor supply enhancement: elevate intracellular L-leucine as the direct precursor of iso-amylamine.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Iso-amylamine production requires L-leucine precursor; leuABCD genes are all involved in L-leucine biosynthesis.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper explicitly states leuABCD were overexpressed to increase the precursor L-leucine because they constitute the L-leucine biosynthesis pathway.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When producing an L-leucine-derived amine from glucose in E. coli, overexpress the leuABCD operon to raise L-leucine precursor supply, because these genes catalyze the committed steps of L-leucine biosynthesis; note that a promiscuous decarboxylase with higher activity toward L-valine will partially divert flux to the valine-derived amine.

experiments.purpose: Enhance iso-butylamine production by scale-up of iBA01 to fed-batch.
experiments.intervention: Fed-batch fermentation in 6.6 L bioreactor (2 L NM3), pH-stat 7.0 with ammonia, DO 40%, glucose feeding when residual glucose < 3 g/L.
experiments.conditions: 30 C; NM3 with L-Ile/L-Leu/D-pantothenate supplementation (auxotrophic host).
experiments.outcome: 8.63 g/L iso-butylamine, productivity 0.21 g/L/h, yield 0.062 g/g (6.50-fold over flask).

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass (fermentation-condition change), Q2 pass, Q3 pass (established the process baseline against which iBA02 was compared).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Fermentation/process step: fed-batch with DO and pH control to boost titer.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: iBA01 showed efficient iso-butylamine production without L-valine byproduct in flask cultivation.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: No explicit rationale given for the specific NM3 formulation, DO setpoint (40%) or feeding trigger; presented as standard process optimization.

experiments.purpose: Remove iBA01 auxotrophies while retaining competing-pathway repression, then produce iso-butylamine without supplementation.
experiments.host: E. coli WLGBH (pKBRilvBNCED) - parental strain of Val with intact ilvA/leuA/panB
experiments.intervention: Synthetic sRNA knockdown of ilvA, leuA and panB via pTac15-vlmDopt-anti-ilvA-leuA-panB (strain iBA02), instead of the gene knockouts used in the Val strain.
experiments.conditions: Fed-batch as EXP-06 but NM3 without L-Ile/L-Leu/D-pantothenate (medium and feed).
experiments.outcome: 10.67 g/L iso-butylamine, productivity 0.36 g/L/h, yield 0.057 g/g (slightly lower than iBA01's 0.062), max OD600 60.5 (59.6% higher than iBA01's 37.9), no amino-acid/vitamin supplementation.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass (sRNA knockdown construct), Q2 pass (plasmid assembled in this study from ref-32 cassettes), Q3 pass (yielded the best-performing, prototrophic production strain).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Competing-pathway blocking: repress ilvA/leuA/panB to redirect flux toward L-valine/iso-butylamine.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: iBA01 (Val chassis) is auxotrophic for L-Ile, L-Leu and D-pantothenate because ilvA, leuA and panB were deleted to remove competing pathways - a critical industrial bioprocess problem.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured fed-batch titer, productivity, yield and cell density improvements.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Stated logic: knockdown rather than knockout retains residual pathway activity, eliminating auxotrophy while still dampening competing fluxes; the sRNA delivery method itself is taken from ref 32.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When competing-pathway knockouts (ilvA, leuA, panB) cause auxotrophies in an L-valine-pathway-derived iso-butylamine production strain, replace them with synthetic sRNA-mediated knockdown of the same genes, because partial repression preserves prototrophic growth while still redirecting carbon flux toward the product.
alternatives_considered: gene knockouts as in Val (pKBRilvBNCED) - rejected because they cause the auxotrophies being solved

experiments.purpose: Improve VlmD activity toward L-alanine to enhance ethylamine production (proof-of-concept enzyme engineering).
experiments.host: E. coli WL3110 (12 strains, each overexpressing one vlmD variant + alaDopt)
experiments.intervention: Rational single-point mutagenesis of VlmD: homology model (SWISS-MODEL, template GAD67 PDB 2OKJ) + PLP-L-alanine docking (AutoDock Vina) identified 6 active-site residues; 12 candidate substitutions (V94I/L, V114I/L, T397A/V, W399L, S431T/V/L, D515K/N) selected from 250 BLASTP homologs; introduced by site-directed mutagenesis.
experiments.conditions: Flask culture as EA01 (MR + 20 g/L glucose, 37 C, 48 h).
experiments.analysis: Mean +/- s.d.; percent improvement vs EA01.
experiments.outcome: Best variant V94I: 5.69 mg/L ethylamine, +96.9% vs EA01 (2.89 mg/L); titer still low in absolute terms.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass (point mutations), Q2 pass, Q3 pass (demonstrated a transferable route to improve VlmD toward poor substrates).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Rate-limiting enzyme engineering: VlmD's low activity toward L-alanine was the identified bottleneck in EA01.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: EA01 secreted more L-alanine (22.78 mg/L) than ethylamine (2.89 mg/L); VlmD showed its lowest in vitro conversion on L-alanine among the 12 working substrates.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Mutation selection rested on a homology model (19.76% sequence identity template) and docking predictions - predictive, required experimental confirmation; confirmation then obtained by flask titers (硬 outcome data), but the design-stage evidence is predictive.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper states an explicit structural mechanism: L-alanine is smaller than VlmD's preferred substrates, so introducing bulkier residues reduces active-site volume and increases interaction probability with PLP-L-alanine.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When a PLP-dependent decarboxylase shows poor activity toward a substrate smaller than its preferred substrates, mutate active-site residues contacting the ligand to bulkier amino acids drawn from homolog-sequence variation, because reducing active-site volume increases contacts with the smaller substrate (demonstrated for VlmD/ethylamine only).

strain.caveat: Full list in Supplementary Table 2 (unavailable); Val strain construction is background_citation (ref 21).

replicates.caveat: replicate_type unresolved (author says only 'triplicates'/'repeated three times').

article_type_gate.rationale: Original Results with novel engineered strains, full Methods, triplicate experiments and Source Data statements; journal research article format (Nature Communications, DOI 10.1038/s41467-020-20423-6).

extensions.engineering_paper_type_rationale: Core contributions are pathway design + precursor-supply/competing-pathway engineering for SCPA overproduction (metabolic_engineering); a final proof-of-concept section applies rational mutagenesis to VlmD (protein_engineering). Biosensor, evolutionary and chassis-redesign strategies absent.

paper_target_strains.paper_strain_normalized: E. coli WL3110 (lacI- derivative of W3110)
paper_target_strains.lineage_or_engineering_context: lacI knockout mutant of W3110, allowing constitutive Ptac expression; host for PA01, EA01 and the 12 VlmD-variant strains
Used only for His-tagged VlmD overexpression/purification (pET-his-vlmDopt)

conflicts.topic: Precursor identity for cyclopentylamine in the in vitro high-activity list
conflicts.prose_interpretation: Results text (results_p006) lists 1-aminocyclohexanecarboxylic acid among high-activity substrates converting to cyclopentylamine.
conflicts.equation_or_figure_interpretation: Fig. 3 caption (results_p032) pairs (j) 1-aminocyclopentanecarboxylic acid -> cyclopentylamine and (k) 1-aminocyclohexanecarboxylic acid -> cyclohexylamine, which is also the chemically consistent assignment.
conflicts.impact: Ambiguous precursor-product pairing for cyclopentylamine in one prose sentence; figure-level data (and chemistry) favor cyclopentane precursor. Does not change titer data.

conflicts.prose_interpretation: results_p049 lists 'L-2-phenylalanine' among poorly converted substrates.
conflicts.equation_or_figure_interpretation: results_p008, methods_p004 and Fig. 3l all use 'L-2-phenylglycine' as the benzylamine precursor.
conflicts.impact: Naming inconsistency only; L-2-phenylglycine is the consistent identity across Methods/Fig. 3.
